first_impression.reaction: Greece is on our list and Crete keeps coming up, so I Googled it. No 'island paradise' opener, just a sorting rule: 'The right area depends on three things: how many guests you are inviting, which kind of ceremony you want, and which airport those guests will land at.' Airport is literally our grandparents question, and it's in the first paragraph. Kept reading.

journey.quote: Exclusive use usually means a chosen space rather than the whole hotel, and curfews and minimum nights are rarely published, so get them in writing before you pay a deposit.
journey.reaction: This is exactly where a surprise invoice comes from. Being told what isn't known up front is more convincing than a glossy promise.

journey.section: Crete wedding venues at a glance (table)
journey.quote: The table runs east to west. It is not a ranking.
journey.reaction: Good. I hate 'best of' lists that are obviously paid placements. This is the table I'd screenshot for James, and the capacity column already rules a few in for 60 to 90.

journey.section: How to compare Crete venues like for like
journey.quote: At Nana Princess it means the chosen room or venue for a symbolic wedding, not the whole resort.
journey.reaction: Lawyer brain approves. A real example of the fine print, not just a warning that fine print exists.

journey.section: How to compare Crete venues like for like
journey.quote: Some venues also set minimums: Abaton's wedding packages ask for at least 10 rooms for at least two nights, depending on guest numbers.
journey.reaction: That's the kind of detail only someone who has read the actual brochure would know. Useful, because half our list would be booking rooms anyway.

journey.quote: Ask how the 2026 works affect your date if you are marrying next season.
journey.reaction: Building works on a wedding day is my nightmare. Honest trade-off, and it makes me trust the nice bits about the other venues more.

journey.quote: Adults only is a decision, not a detail. If nieces, nephews or godchildren are on the list, this one is out.
journey.reaction: Blunt and correct. We have three nieces, so that's one off the board in five seconds.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms capacity, exclusive use, curfew and minimum nights in writing for any venue on this coast.
journey.reaction: By the Heraklion coast I'd read some version of this line four or five times. I got it the first time. It starts to feel like a template, and a bit like being sold to between every section.

journey.quote: Australians entering the Schengen area for a short stay now have fingerprints and a photo taken under the European Entry/Exit System.
journey.reaction: Useful, but it's under 'Transfers for guests' and it's about border control. I came to this heading wanting coaches and drive times and got passport queues first.

journey.section: Getting to Crete for your wedding
journey.quote: Booking guests into the wrong airport is the costliest mistake on Crete. Minos Beach and Minos Palace both put Chania Airport about three hours away.
journey.reaction: This goes straight to Mum and Dad. Three hours on a coach after a long-haul flight would finish my grandparents off.

journey.quote: None of this rules out a summer wedding. It means shade for the ceremony, an indoor fallback for every outdoor space, and travel insurance that every guest has read.
journey.reaction: Wildfires and earthquakes mentioned calmly, with what to actually do about them. The ceremony-time table by month is the kind of thing I'd never have thought to ask.

journey.quote: It states that the marriage must then be registered at the Registry Office in Aghios Nikolaos within 40 days. Keep a weekday free in the itinerary.
journey.reaction: Within 40 days, but keep a weekday free? Do we personally have to be there to register it, or is that done for us after we've flown home? I can't tell.

journey.quote: Spring and autumn ceremonies can start earlier in the day.
journey.reaction: The question was when is the best time to marry. This answers what time of day, not which months. Minor, but it reads like it dodged the question.

journey.section: Shortlist your Crete venues with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is one person, start to finish, who works in your time zone and quotes in AUD.
journey.reaction: One person and AUD quotes go at two of my fears: being passed around, and currency surprises. Still doesn't say who is physically there on the day.

unanswered_questions: Is our Wedded Advisor, or someone you are accountable for, physically in Crete on the wedding day, or do you hand over to a local planner we've never met?
Is there a real wedding you've planned at one of these 15 venues, with the venue and date, that I can look at?
For 60 to 90 guests with half flying in from Australia, which two or three of these would you actually shortlist?
Do you book the guest coaches and airport transfers, or just advise on them?
For a civil ceremony, do we need to be present for the registration at the Registry Office, or is it done for us after we leave?

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms room counts, ceremony options, exclusive use and curfew in writing for every venue in the west.
turn_offs_found.why: Each line on its own is fine and even reassuring, but repeated after nearly every area on top of three linked CTAs, it starts to read as a sales nudge between sections rather than advice. It's the template feel that makes me wonder if a person is really behind it.

would_share_with: James (partner): the at-a-glance table and the exclusive-use explanation, so we can cross off venues by capacity together
Mum and Dad (contributing): the airport section, especially the three-hour Chania warning, and the summer heat and wildfire paragraph
Our parents again: the legal section, so they understand the paperwork timeline and why a symbolic ceremony isn't legally binding

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [shortlist your Crete venues with a Wedded Advisor](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=crete-wedding-venues&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: 'When you are ready' is the right tone, not pushy. But I'd want to see one real Crete or Greece wedding you've done and read one more post before handing over our details.

top_3_changes: Cut most of the repeated 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms ... in writing' closers after each area; say it once strongly (the house-rules paragraph already does) and let the venue detail do the work.
Move the Entry/Exit System paragraph out of 'Transfers for guests' (or rename the heading) so the transfers section leads with coaches and drive times.
Clarify whether the couple must attend the Registry Office registration within 40 days, and make the 'best time' FAQ answer which months, not just which hours.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Sophie (planner_couple), using persona voice and concerns
No invented brand facts; missing details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments and VERIFY markers ignored
Title, business details and absent prices treated as not must-fix; no requests for sourcing lines, per orchestrator

open_questions.question: The legal section says registration is within 40 days but also says 'Keep a weekday free in the itinerary'. Worth an editor check that the source supports the couple needing to attend in person?

assumptions: Arrived from a Google search for 'crete wedding venues' during early destination research; no other context was given.
Skimmed venues that can't hold 60 to 90 or are adults only; read the table, comparison, airport, season and legal sections closely.
Family details (grandparents, nieces, parents contributing) are persona colour, not brand facts.
The persona card is provisional (not CRM-calibrated).
